processing: Local seed-grown leaf is withered at length and dried without firing or rolling, and sorted into Xiao Bai needle, gong mei and shou mei.
harvest_season: Spring for buds and gong mei, with later, more mature leaf for shou mei; specific local dates are little documented.
appearance_dry: Small, slim shoots shaped rather like eyebrows, less showy and less plump than big-white teas.
appearance_liquor: Clear pale gold, deepening in the coarser grades.
appearance_wet: Small, narrow, uneven leaves, as you would expect from a seed-grown population.
taste_profile: Fresh and clean with a distinct aroma and a clear sweet finish, lighter in body than big-white cultivars.

brewing.notes: Small leaf infuses fast, so keep early steeps shorter than for big-white teas. Taste before lengthening.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year under grades such as Xiao Bai Gong Mei and Xiao Bai Shou Mei. As usual for Fujian white tea, it may be drunk young or stored, but keeping behaviour specific to Xiao Bai is little documented. Small output means it is rarer than big-white teas.
description:
Xiao Bai means small white, and that is the difference: it comes from local Cai Cha, seed-grown plants, rather than from the big-white clones behind most Fuding and Zhenghe tea. Jianyang, in northern Fujian, is its home, and Zhangdun is the township most associated with it.

It is made the usual white tea way, by long withering and drying. The shoots are smaller and less uniform, and yield is lower, so it cannot compete on looks with a downy Fuding needle.

What it offers is in the cup: a fresh, clean taste with its own aroma and a clear, sweet finish. The small leaf gives up flavour quickly, so short steeps tend to work better than the long ones used for big-white buds.

Look for the grade name, since gong mei and shou mei made from Xiao Bai are the common forms. Compare it with a big-white peony to see how much the plant matters in a white tea made almost the same way.
history: Xiao Bai is tied to Jianyang, which is described as its place of origin, and to the older distinction between white tea from local Cai Cha plants and from big-white plants. Its exact starting date is not established. Zhangdun, with the largest area and output, has been promoted as the home of Xiao Bai, and a local Jianyang standard now names its grades.
